title: JSFL runtime: doc.align, doc.distributeToLayers, doc.transformSelection are no-op stubs — blocks automated layout workflows
description:
File: packages/authoring-ui/src/jsfl/runtime.ts.

Three commonly-used JSFL authoring methods are no-op stubs:
- doc.align() (line ~1878): aligns selected objects to each other or to the stage. Emits console.warn('doc.align: not implemented').
- doc.distributeToLayers() (line ~1882): distributes selected objects to separate layers. No-op stub.
- doc.transformSelection() (line ~3000): applies a 2×2 transform matrix to the current selection. Emits console.warn.

These are all frequently used in automated JSFL scripts for layout and organisation. Any agent workflow that calls fl.getDocumentDOM().align('left edge') or distributes objects to layers will silently do nothing.

Priority:
- doc.align: HIGH impact for layout scripts. Real Flash JSFL: doc.align(alignMode, boolAlignToStage). alignModes: 'left edge', 'right edge', 'top edge', 'bottom edge', 'center horizontal', 'center vertical'. Implementation should compute the bounding box of selected objects and shift each to match the desired alignment axis.
- doc.distributeToLayers: MEDIUM impact. Moves each selected object to its own new layer. Common pattern for animating multi-object groups.
- doc.transformSelection: LOWER impact (usually for programmatic transforms; agents prefer stage_update).

Suggested implementation for doc.align: resolve selected objects in the active frame, compute their bounding boxes using transformedShapeBounds/x,y, determine the alignment target (leftmost x, rightmost x, top y, etc. or stage bounds when boolAlignToStage=true), then mutate each object's x or y field in the doc model. Push via pushDoc.
